title: high latency when rebuilding graphQL schema after addClass
body:
After creating 2000 classes, the addClass API becomes very slow, around 10sec. CPU profiling shows the majority of time is spent on buildGraphQLSchema. Since there is [a single lock for addClass](https://github.com/weaviate/weaviate/blob/master/usecases/schema/add.go#L121-L122), all other addClass ends up waiting in the queue. I guess buildGraphQLSchema latency glows linearly with the number of classes in the system. 

This single lock and slow buildGraphQLSchema latency prevents us from using Weaviate with many classes, especially in multi-tenant environments. I there a workaround to speed up buildGraphQLSchema or avoid the single lock?


CPU profile flame graph
![Screenshot 2023-05-09 at 10 58 32 AM](https://github.com/weaviate/weaviate/assets/1431459/c35e7959-f66e-4fd4-ab60-15cee9a8800e)

CPU pprof profile raw data:
[profile.cpu.txt](https://github.com/weaviate/weaviate/files/11434593/profile.cpu.txt)

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: This issue is really blocking up as we are not able to keep low single digit thousand classes active in a Weaviate instance due to create and delete class latency going through the roof (exponential increase with number of active project). Would really appreciate any help in debugging/mitigating this.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: In case you can't wait for #2970 we could consider a short-term fix, such as rebuilding the GraphQL schema async (throttled). It won't make the rebuild itself faster, but it would decouple the generation from adding classes.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
If it helps, attaching a dump of schema after we added ~300 classes.

[schema.json.zip](https://github.com/weaviate/weaviate/files/11444980/schema.json.zip)

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
@participant2 Thanks for the short term fix proposal. We are looking to get Weaviate in production for our upcoming product launch by end of this month and hence the urgency.

Wanted to validate the rebuild latency expectation to ensure that our setup isn't broken/misconfigured. Is saveSchema() expected to take 10s of secs as number of classes reach low single digit thousands?

Our usecase is, addClass -> add_data_object -> query -..(some point in future)..-> deleteClass (to keep working set of classes in Weaviate below some threshold).

What will be implication of async graphql schema rebuild on add_data_object and query?

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: We are running Weaviate 1.18.4 release with 12 CPU cores, 48G RAM and PV backed by [EBS gp3 volume](https://<redacted-host>/ebs/general-purpose/). In this setup, we are not bottlenecked on CPU, memory, IO.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: also, our data schema is simple and the query is fixed. If there is a quick way to disable the graphQL API and schema update, we could use RESTful API to call the db layer to avoid paying the cost of graphQL.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
> also, our data schema is simple and the query is fixed. If there is a quick way to disable the graphQL API and schema update, we could use RESTful API to call the db layer to avoid paying the cost of graphQL.

I was about to propose the same. We've recently added a gRPC API for a similar purpose. What language (client) are you using to query? We already added some gRPC support to the python client, but could also quickly extend one of the other languages. 

PS: We can also discuss that in a call whenever this suits you / there is an email thread already going on for this. Would be great if the two you could join the proposed call – I'll make sure to do the same.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
> Currently, we are only using python client (we have some active prototype being done from a golang service).

This is excellent news. This means we could likely just deactivate GraphQL, and you could just use gRPC already. If not, then we can extend the missing endpoints on short notice. We don't have gRPC support in the Golang client yet, but it's great to know that this would be the next language you'd need, so we can plan ahead on that front.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
Updates:

- We've identified the leak described in #2981 and have a fix ready (not merged/released yet)
- We've prepared an option to disable GraphQL (relying solely on gRPC)

We're currently reviewing and merging everything, including extending the gRPC API that can be used as an alternative to GraphQL. Let's discuss which exact functionality you need. We should have an end-2-end flow ready with all of the above before the end of this week.
